title: Fire Protection — Cargo Compartment Extinguishing — Third Metering Stage for Extended Diversion
abstract: Addition of a third metering stage and re-balancing of the cargo extinguishing distribution manifold, extending the sustaining discharge from 180 to 240 minutes without adding bottle capacity.

sections.planning_reason: Operators opening South Atlantic and mid-Pacific routings needed a 240-minute diversion approval, and on this aircraft the limiting item is the cargo compartment suppression duration rather than any propulsion or systems item. The existing installation meters the knock-down and sustaining flows in two stages sized for 180 minutes. Adding bottle capacity costs weight and floor space, so the distribution is re-balanced instead and a third low-rate stage carries the final hour.
sections.description: A third metering orifice stage is added downstream of the existing pair and the distribution manifold is re-balanced so that both compartments still reach the sustaining concentration within 45 seconds. The distribution pump is re-worked with a smaller impeller, the concentration sensor is replaced by a unit with a wider range and the forward heat exchanger is deleted because the third stage runs cool enough not to need it. Nozzle positions do not change.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Discharge and remove the extinguishing bottles to the standard practice. WARNING: THE BOTTLES ARE PRESSURISED. DO NOT REMOVE A BOTTLE UNTIL THE SAFETY PIN IS INSTALLED. Get access in the cargo compartments and the belly fairing, zones 133, 142 and 183. Re-work the upper distribution pump D2620124013196 with the smaller impeller from the kit. Replace the aft distribution sensor D2620124813243 by the wider range unit. Remove the forward heat exchanger D2620125756547 and blank the ports. Install the third metering orifice block downstream of the existing pair, retaining it with anchor nuts AES155061-5B and barrel nuts AES9630K5, and close the pipe joints with swaged collars LN413515-8E. Re-rate the right-hand switch position 1394WF2, the left-hand heat exchanger position 58WF and the left-hand non-return valve position 6WF4 to the revised flow using the setting table in the accomplishment instructions. Install the bottles. Do AMM-S-26-20-12-700-016-A as the concentration test in both compartments and record the measured concentration at 45 seconds, at 180 minutes and at 240 minutes. Record the embodiment and apply for the revised diversion approval.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to twin-engine aircraft from MSN S00669 up to the production cut-in at MSN S01632. Two aircraft are excluded because they carry a different compartment lining standard that changes the volume assumption behind the metering. Aircraft from MSN S01632 onward already have the third stage.
sections.material_note: Kit K2620-1009-01 contains the orifice block, the impeller, the sensor and the fastener set. Lead time is eighteen weeks. The concentration test agent is supplied separately and has a twelve-month shelf life, so it should be ordered against a confirmed slot rather than held.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's discretion, before the extended diversion approval is required. There is no compliance deadline.
